subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should OpenClaw keep this issue as the umbrella for cron/session guardrails now that the warning PR closed unmerged, or narrow it to the source-reproduced retention bug and split warning/context UX separately?
rationale: The retention bug is source-reproducible, but fixed warning thresholds and context-pressure UX are user-facing product policy choices not settled by the open retention PR.

options.title: Keep umbrella open
options.body: Use this issue to coordinate retention cleanup plus warning/context diagnostics until maintainers decide which pieces ship together.

options.title: Split after retention lands
options.body: Let the retention PR address the source-repro bug, then create or confirm separate issues for high-frequency warnings and context-pressure diagnostics.

options.title: Narrow to retention only
options.body: Declare warnings and threshold UX out of scope here and close this issue only when the retention bug is fixed.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella open
recommendation.body: Use this issue to coordinate retention cleanup plus warning/context diagnostics until maintainers decide which pieces ship together.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily the cron/session lifecycle and cleanup contract introduced and maintained in the session maintenance history.
